S6SD01117.name: Brian Bengs
S6SD01117.bio: Former Navy sailor, Air Force officer and judge advocate (JAG) who has also worked as a military prosecutor, federal ethics advisor and National Park Ranger.

positions.stance: Says it is "long past time for the ultra-rich to pay their fair share once again" and that taxes can be lowered for small businesses and working people.
Calls balancing the federal budget and paying down the national debt "imperatives" and suggests withholding congressional salaries during a government shutdown.
Says members of Congress and their spouses "must be banned from purchasing, selling, or holding individual stocks" while in office.
Opposes corporate PACs and mega-donors spending unlimited money to "drown out the voices of everyday Americans."
Calls for halting construction of new data centers and says communities need the right to say no to AI data center development.

ca-gov-2026-becerra-xavier.name: Xavier Becerra
ca-gov-2026-becerra-xavier.bio: Former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services, California Attorney General, member of Congress and State Assembly member.

positions.stance: Calls health care "a human right"; pledges to strengthen Medi-Cal and "build toward a universal single-payer system that puts people before profits."
Vows to "protect and lead our state against Trump and his attacks as Governor," citing his record suing the administration as Attorney General.
Says he will "treat housing like the essential infrastructure it is" and build more affordable homes.
Pledges to stand up to "price gouging and unjustified rate hikes," expand help with childcare, and use state power to lower prices where markets have failed.
Supports treating clean energy and grid resilience "as public investments" so renters, low-income households and workers share the benefits.

ca-gov-2026-hilton-steve.name: Steve Hilton
ca-gov-2026-hilton-steve.bio: Author, broadcaster and Silicon Valley founder; former senior advisor to UK Prime Minister David Cameron, Stanford instructor and host of Fox News' The Next Revolution.

positions.stance: Promises "$3.00 Gas" by ending "the rules and fees that drove California gas prices through the roof."
Pledges to "Cut Utility Bills in Half" by taking on "the political mandates and failures that made electricity unaffordable."
Proposes "eliminating state income tax on the first $150,000" earned by working Californians.
Pledges to "clear out the red tape, fees and bad rules" that made starter homes for young families too expensive to build.
Says "Every Student Reads by 3rd Grade" and pledges to make early literacy a top priority.

ca-ltgov-2026-ma-fiona.name: Fiona Ma
ca-ltgov-2026-ma-fiona.bio: California State Treasurer and CPA; previously served on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, in the California Assembly and on the State Board of Equalization.

positions.stance: Pledges to "grow our economy, attract investment, and create high-quality jobs."
Says she will "work to make college more affordable."
Pledges to "ensure seniors can age with dignity."
Says she "will continue the fight for healthcare access for everyone."
Pledges to "champion our first responders and public safety personnel" so people feel safe in their homes, at work and on the streets.

ca-ltgov-2026-romero-gloria.name: Gloria Romero
ca-ltgov-2026-romero-gloria.bio: Former California State Senate Majority Leader and Assembly Majority Whip, and Professor Emeritus at Cal State Los Angeles.

positions.stance: Pledges to "restore merit in admissions, protect academic standards, and stop setting students up for failure."
Says Jewish students and students of every faith and background "deserve safety, dignity, and equal treatment on campus."
Says she "will proudly stand up for women's sports and Title IX."
Will push for "serious oversight, real consequences, and basic accountability" to stop fraud in the community college application system.
Pledges to be "a strong, common-sense voice for fire prevention, smarter land management, and faster rebuilding" and to streamline state commissions.
Proposes letting voters decide, by constitutional amendment, to eliminate school district property taxes on homeowners, and lowering the homestead appraisal cap from 10% to 3%.
Says "cutting red tape and expanding the housing supply will make housing more affordable for all Texans," including third-party inspections and pre-approved home designs.
Supports "lowering out-of-pocket healthcare costs by capping co-pays and lowering insurance premiums."
Says "lowering the cost of home and auto insurance benefits all Texans."
Supports "increasing competition in the energy market" to save customers and small businesses thousands per year.

tx-gov-2026-hinojosa-gina.name: Gina Hinojosa
tx-gov-2026-hinojosa-gina.bio: Former civil rights and union lawyer and Austin ISD School Board president who went on to serve in the Texas House.

positions.stance: Pledges to "end the STAAR test and tests like it, pause the rigged A-F accountability system," and seek a bill creating real accountability.
Will "return school districts that have been taken over back to their communities."
Rejects spending on school vouchers and pledges to "end the voucher scam" so tax dollars go to neighborhood schools.
Pledges on day one to replace TEA Commissioner Mike Morath and "appoint an educator to lead the Texas Education Agency."
Will "audit and terminate corrupt vendor contracts" and use the money to make teachers among the highest paid in the nation.
Listed "Providing School Choice" (Senate Bill 2) among his top priority bills for the 2025 legislative session.
Listed "Banning THC in Texas" (Senate Bill 3) among his top priority bills for the 2025 legislative session.
Listed "Increasing the Homestead Exemption to $140,000" (Senate Bill 4) among his top 2025 priority bills.
Listed establishing a Dementia Prevention & Research Institute of Texas (Senate Bill 5) among his top 2025 priority bills.
Listed "Increasing Texas' Electric Grid Reliability" (Senate Bill 6) among his top 2025 priority bills.

tx-ltgov-2026-goodwin-vikki.name: Vikki Goodwin
tx-ltgov-2026-goodwin-vikki.bio: State representative serving her fourth term in the Texas Legislature, representing parts of Austin and the Lake Travis area.

positions.stance: Proposes "Texas Cares," a new state-administered health insurance program to create coverage options for the 5.1 million uninsured Texans.
Supports "a well-funded, efficient system of free public schools — not vouchers for the wealthy"; says tax money shouldn't go to religious schools.
Says Texans deserve "clean and healthy water" and "reliable energy" and that "corporations should take a back seat to Texas families."
Supports increasing the supply of homes and apartments, keeping rents down and limiting tax increases.
Says Texans deserve "comprehensive, affordable healthcare" and should be able to see doctors and specialists without fighting for coverage.

fl-gov-2026-donalds-byron.name: Byron Donalds
fl-gov-2026-donalds-byron.bio: Member of Congress for Florida's 19th Congressional District and former Florida House member.

positions.stance: Says Florida "cannot become too expensive for working families and seniors on fixed incomes" and that "it's time to bring down costs."
Says "you deserve to know what healthcare costs before you get treated"; proposes a "Your Doctor, Your Price" plan to cut red tape.
Says "bureaucratic delays shouldn't stop honest people from opening a business and earning a living."
Says "reading by third grade is a basic promise every child deserves" and supports a debt-free route to a great-paying job.
Says "we must secure our borders," keep neighborhoods safe, "stop taxpayer handouts to illegal immigration, and keep deadly drugs off our streets."

fl-gov-2026-jolly-david.name: David Jolly
fl-gov-2026-jolly-david.bio: Former Member of Congress and attorney.

positions.stance: Proposes a state catastrophic fund that "removes natural disaster risk from the private insurance market" to reduce property and car insurance costs.
Says Florida "should commit to expanding Medicaid and ensuring healthcare for all Floridians."
Calls for dramatically increasing investment in public schools and more competitive teacher pay; says voucher schools should meet the same standards as public schools.
Says "Florida needs an immediate moratorium on the construction of hyperscale data centers, issued on day one."
Says Florida "should lead the nation in campaign finance reform" and pass a sweeping ethics package committed to transparency.
Says she is "working to deliver universal child care" and lists statewide universal pre-K and free school meals for every student.
Says she is working to "lower auto insurance costs."
Pledges to "invest in keeping NY streets and subways safe," citing stronger red flag laws and a crackdown on retail theft and hate crimes.
Cites "cutting middle-class taxes to the lowest rate in 70 years" and "tripling the New York child tax credit" as steps to make the state affordable.
Says "she's standing up to Trump," citing lawsuits over tariffs, holding ICE agents accountable and protecting abortion rights in New York.

ny-gov-2026-blakeman-bruce.name: Bruce A. Blakeman
ny-gov-2026-blakeman-bruce.bio: Two-term Nassau County Executive and former Port Authority Commissioner.

positions.stance: Says that as County Executive he "said NO to Kathy Hochul's sanctuary policies, and worked with ICE to take criminals off our streets."
Cites hiring hundreds of new police and law enforcement officers in Nassau County and describes "a no-nonsense approach to fighting crime."
Says "as Governor, he will deliver real relief to homeowners and renters," citing not raising property or sales taxes as County Executive.

pa-gov-2026-shapiro-josh.name: Josh Shapiro
pa-gov-2026-shapiro-josh.bio: Governor of Pennsylvania; previously Pennsylvania Attorney General, Chair of the Montgomery County Board of Commissioners and State Representative.

pa-gov-2026-garrity-stacy.name: Stacy Garrity
pa-gov-2026-garrity-stacy.bio: Pennsylvania State Treasurer, retired U.S. Army Reserve Colonel and former business executive at Global Tungsten & Powders Corp.

positions.stance: Pledges on day one to "lift the ban on new drilling sites" and call a special session to fast-track permits for natural gas, pipelines and power plants.
Proposes cutting taxes and hidden costs on electric bills, including rolling back or eliminating the gross receipts tax on utilities.
Proposes a "HOPE for PA" initiative to cut the property tax burden by one-third within two years and cover up to 3% of first-time buyers' mortgage interest.
Supports passing voter ID: "It should be easy to vote and hard to cheat. Every voter should be a U.S. citizen and show ID."
Says parents "need to be in control of their children's education" and supports Lifeline Scholarships and expanding existing state scholarship programs.
Says he "has made it his mission to make life more affordable," citing eliminating the state grocery tax and creating a state Child Tax Credit.
"Believes healthcare is a right, not a privilege"; cites lowering prescription drug costs and eliminating over $1 billion in medical debt.
Says he is "leading a national fight against Donald Trump's attacks on education, healthcare, and the economy."
Cites a climate law putting Illinois "on the path to 100% clean energy by 2050" and efforts to make Illinois a leader in quantum technology.
Says he has made "the fight for economic and social justice a top priority," citing expanded voting rights and cannabis record expungements.

il-gov-2026-bailey-darren.name: Darren Bailey
il-gov-2026-bailey-darren.bio: Third-generation farmer and former Illinois state representative and state senator who served 17 years on the North Clay Board of Education.

positions.stance: Will fight to ensure "schools are fully funded, empower parents to make the best choices for their children, and support teachers."
Pledges to "stand with law enforcement, not against them," hold violent criminals accountable and crack down on repeat offenders.
Will "fight to lower taxes, cut wasteful government spending, and bring real fiscal responsibility back to Springfield."
Says "no family should ever pay more in property taxes than their mortgage" and pledges to rein in government waste and deliver real tax relief.

ga-gov-2026-jackson-rick.name: Rick Jackson
ga-gov-2026-jackson-rick.bio: Georgia businessman and philanthropist who built a health care company.

positions.stance: Pledges to "freeze property taxes immediately," "cut the state income tax in half within 4 years," and freeze public college tuition, room and board.
Pledges to recruit jobs statewide, support small businesses and "make Georgia the #1 state for entrepreneurship in America."
Will provide cost-effective capital options for farmers and help them negotiate better prices for key materials and equipment.
Supports tying public assistance "to work or job training for able-bodied adults"; says government assistance "should be a bridge, not a lifestyle."
Pledges to "audit every government program for results and effectiveness" and "eliminate programs that don't work."
Pledges to lower health care costs "by expanding Medicaid, ending the failed Georgia Pathways program, and replacing it with real coverage."
Proposes a Georgia Housing Fast Track initiative to streamline permitting, expanded down payment and renter assistance, and an affordable housing trust fund.
Pledges to "fully fund Georgia's schools and modernize the state's outdated education funding formula"; supports eliminating state income tax for teachers.
Will help families keep and grow their land and "fight to support farmers harmed by Trump's tariffs and trade chaos."
Proposes an Office of Small Business focused on firms with 0 to 25 employees and expanded state small business loan and grant programs.

ga-ltgov-2026-dolezal-greg.name: Greg Dolezal
ga-ltgov-2026-dolezal-greg.bio: Georgia state senator and businessman who has built companies in Georgia.

positions.stance: Will "fight for secure borders, fair trade, and policies that put American workers and families ahead of global interests."
Says rising property values "shouldn't mean ever-increasing tax bills" and that school taxes should go away once homeowners turn 65.
Says the best way to grow the economy "is to lower taxes for everyone, not have politicians play investment banker," while investing in infrastructure.
Says "parents, not bureaucrats, should be in charge of their children's education"; authored a broad school choice bill.
Says "American homes should be for American families"; wrote legislation to ban hedge fund and foreign ownership of single-family homes.

ga-ltgov-2026-mclaurin-josh.name: Josh McLaurin
ga-ltgov-2026-mclaurin-josh.bio: Georgia state senator serving his fourth term in the legislature and an attorney.

positions.stance: Will push to "reinvest state revenues into the needs of working families" such as child care and housing instead of corporate tax breaks.
Will "stand with labor to protect the right to organize"; criticizes Georgia's "right to work" laws.
Committed to passing laws that prohibit discrimination "of all kinds" and protect minority voting power.
Will "fight to expand coverage" through Medicaid expansion and make care accessible across the state.
Will work to overturn Georgia's 6-week abortion ban; says "personal health decisions should remain between patients and their doctors."

mi-gov-2026-benson-jocelyn.name: Jocelyn Benson
mi-gov-2026-benson-jocelyn.bio: Michigan Secretary of State, civil rights advocate and former law school dean.

positions.stance: Her "Affordable Michigan agenda" would streamline construction regulations, incentivize starter homes and crack down on corporate investors "who buy up properties and drive up rents."
Says "housing is the foundation for economic security" and "as Governor, I will make it a top priority."
Says "healthcare should be a right, not a privilege" and that Michigan's Department of Health and Human Services must be fixed so people can access resources.
Says Michigan has "a childcare affordability crisis" and pledges a system providing "every child a strong start from day one."
Says "as governor I will use every tool available to me to bring our energy costs down"; refuses contributions from energy companies and corporate PACs.

mi-gov-2026-james-john.name: John James
mi-gov-2026-james-john.bio: Member of Congress, West Point graduate and former U.S. Army Ranger-qualified aviation officer who worked in his family's Michigan business.

positions.stance: Would "hold regulated residential bill growth at or below inflation," tie utility profits to reliability, and repeal PA 235 for an all-of-the-above energy strategy.
Proposes a Parents' Bill of Rights saying parents "have the primary right to direct the education, moral, and religious upbringing of their children."
Says he will "FULLY FUND law enforcement, Back The Blue, and get activist prosecutors and judges out of the way of public safety."
Proposes a "Freedom from Corruption Agenda" and pledges to publicly disclose all of his personal finances as Governor.
Proposes a "family-first, freedom-first, prevention-first agenda" to lower health costs, expand access, protect informed consent and improve food quality.

az-gov-2026-hobbs-katie.name: Katie Hobbs
az-gov-2026-hobbs-katie.bio: Governor of Arizona; former Arizona Secretary of State and social worker.

az-gov-2026-biggs-andy.name: Andy Biggs
az-gov-2026-biggs-andy.bio: Member of Congress representing Arizona's 5th District since 2016.

positions.stance: Proposes "eliminating the state income tax and working with local entities to reduce the property tax burden."
Pledges to "rid waste, fraud, and abuse from state government by reviewing each agency and program" and to ban foreign contributions to campaigns.
Would equip law enforcement to combat drug trafficking and reintroduce a Border Strike Force focused on human and drug trafficking.
Would develop a long-term water strategy and "fight for every drop of our allocated Colorado River water."
Would "protect Empowerment Scholarship Accounts so families can choose the educational method that best meets the needs of their child."
Says she "eliminated renters' fees and is building 100,000 new homes to lower the cost of housing."
Says she is "the first Governor to cap health care deductibles and co-pays."
Says she opposed utility rate increases and launched an Energy Affordability Agenda that "will take $13 billion off your energy bills."
Says she "transformed our veterans' homes to give our vets the care they deserve."
Says she "protected SNAP from federal cuts to feed kids and families."

ma-gov-2026-minogue-michael.name: Michael Roger Minogue
ma-gov-2026-minogue-michael.bio: Combat veteran and business leader who led Abiomed.

positions.stance: Would "audit the state legislature and the entire state budget with an outside auditor" and create a real-time state spending dashboard.
Would cut taxes and spending through audits and "cut state-mandated energy utility fees on day one."
Would "cancel the unfunded, unachievable Net Zero mandate" and pursue natural gas pipelines and modular nuclear options.
Would grow jobs by retaining and recruiting businesses, opt into the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, and "expand charter, tech, vocational schools."
Would "prioritize removing violent criminals and drug dealers and end sanctuary state policies," and eliminate cashless bail.

tn-gov-2026-blackburn-marsha.name: Marsha Blackburn
tn-gov-2026-blackburn-marsha.bio: U.S. Senator from Tennessee and former member of the Tennessee State Senate.

positions.stance: Says she "will work to ensure we keep taxes and prices low and reduce unnecessary spending and regulations" to attract companies to Tennessee.
Says "men have no place in a girls' locker room or on the same sports field" and pledges to protect girls' sports as Governor.
Backs President Trump's immigration policy "100 percent" and will work to ensure "sanctuary cities never have a home in Tennessee."
Says she will "remove do-nothing, Soros-funded, District Attorneys and stand up to those who would try to defund the police."
Says that as Governor "she will fight to protect Tennessee farmers from Communist China," including stopping China from buying farmland.

tn-gov-2026-green-jerri.name: Jerri Green
tn-gov-2026-green-jerri.bio: Lawyer serving District 2 on the Memphis City Council; former juvenile public defender and senior policy advisor to the Shelby County Mayor.

positions.stance: Supports "paid family leave," "affordable child care" and "a real living wage."
Supports "fully funded classrooms," respected teachers and "honest education—not censorship and political interference."
Supports a government that "expands Medicaid, especially in rural Tennessee," and respects a woman's decisions about her own health.
Supports "background checks," "red flag laws" and "gun locks" so "no parent should fear sending their child to school."
Supports "clean air, safe water, and climate-smart policies that protect our land."

md-gov-2026-moore-wes.name: Wes Moore
md-gov-2026-moore-wes.bio: Governor of Maryland; combat veteran, author and former CEO of the Robin Hood Foundation.

positions.stance: Cites over 55,000 new Maryland businesses and major economic investments as evidence his administration "jumpstarted Maryland's economy."
Cites a 44% drop in homicides statewide, "driven by historic funding for law enforcement and public safety resources."
Says his administration delivered record public school funding for four consecutive years, including "a $10.2 billion investment in K-12 education this year."
Says he "cut taxes for the middle-class" and closed a projected shortfall "with no new taxes or fees."
Says he is "lowering energy costs for Maryland families while investing in a cleaner, more reliable energy future."
